3. A signed approximation can yield full samples without an output-length loss

There is a useful generative consequence of the patch compiler that does not require its numerical map to be CP.

Let $p$ be the true joint law, and suppose one has constructed a single real signed law $q$ satisfying
$\sum_y q(y)=1,
\qquad
\|p-q\|_1\le\delta.$
Assume the prefix masses of this same $q$ can be contracted in paid rational arithmetic.

At a reached prefix $v$, define
$s(v)=\sum_a q(va)_+,
\qquad
Q(a\mid v)=\frac{q(va)_+}{s(v)}.$
Because $q(\varnothing)=1$, every reached prefix has $q(v)>0$. Hence $s(v)\ge q(v)>0$, so no zero denominator is reached.

For a reached leaf,
$Q(y)
=
q(y)\prod_{v\prec y}\frac{q(v)}{s(v)}
\le q(y)_+.$
Write $\alpha_-=\sum_y q(y)_-$. Since $Q$ is normalized and is pointwise dominated by $q_+$,
$\|Q-q\|_1=2\alpha_-.$
Both $p$ and $q$ have mass one, so
$2\alpha_-\le\|p-q\|_1.$
Therefore
$\boxed{\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)\le\|p-q\|_1\le\delta.}
\tag{3}$
There is no factor proportional to the number of outputs in (3).

The global consistency of $q$ is essential. Unrelated additive estimates of tiny prefixes do not satisfy this premise.

For the numerical channel, exact trace preservation is restored algebraically by
$\Upsilon
=
\widetilde\Phi+
E_{\mathrm{all}}\circ(\mathrm{Id}-\widetilde\Phi),
\qquad
E_{\mathrm{all}}(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(X)\frac{I}{2^N}.$
This doubles the diamond-error bound at most and adds only polynomial MPO overhead. It is a numerical correction to the approximation, not a physical reset added to the dynamics. Real Pauli coefficients preserve Hermiticity.

Applying $\Upsilon$ to the supplied product state and contracting the supplied POVMs yields the required normalized signed $q$.

For worst-case random-bit work, if site $i$ has $m_i$ outcomes, use
$R=\left\lceil
\log_2\frac{4\sum_i m_i}{\epsilon}
\right\rceil$
random bits per categorical draw. The total coin-rounding TV error is at most $\epsilon/4$. There is no rejection loop and no inverse-minimum-probability runtime. Rational contractions and divisions use their actual numerator and denominator bit lengths.

This gives an end-to-end joint patch sampler. Its general-volume cost remains (1).
